Set
\[
 a_0=\frac{\min\{B,L,1\}}{64},\qquad
 \bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd},
 \qquad q_0=(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}.
\]
Because \(B>0\) and \(L>0\), we have \(a_0>0\).  We first verify,
condition by condition, that the law constructed in
\texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} is a member of the class in
\texttt{def:panel-model-class}.

For the donor law, \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} gives
\[
 \Sigma=\frac12 I_{Sd}
       +\frac{1}{2Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}^{\top}.
\]
The eigenvalue in the direction \(\mathbf 1_{Sd}\) is one, while the
eigenvalue on its orthogonal complement is one half.  Thus \(\Sigma\) is
positive definite, \(q_0>0\), and the displayed restrictions
\(c_\Sigma\le 1/2\) and \(C_\Sigma\ge 1\) imply
\[
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}.
\]
This proves \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Every off-diagonal entry that
exists equals \(1/(2Sd)>0\); in particular, when \(Sd\ge2\), the covariance
has nonzero cross-coordinate or cross-cohort entries.

The vectors \((U_j)_{j=1}^{N}\) are independent and identically distributed,
\(\mathbb E[U_j]=0\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(U_j)=I_{Sd}\).  Since the
square root in the construction is the symmetric positive square root,
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)
 =\Sigma^{1/2}I_{Sd}\Sigma^{1/2}=\Sigma.
\]
Hence \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and
\texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness} hold.  Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[
   \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\mid z_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E[\|U_j\|_2^4]
 =(Sd)^2\le B^4,
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.

We next check the outcome and causal restrictions.  Both displayed formulas
for \(m_1\) give \(m_1(z_{01})=4a_0\), and
\(m_s(z_{0s})=4a_0\) for \(s>1\).  Therefore
\[
 B_{si}(0)\in\{3a_0,5a_0\},
 \qquad
 B_{si}(1)\in\{4a_0,6a_0\}.
\]
In particular \(B_{si}(a)>0\), so
\(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), as required by the support of a simple
return.  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level}, \(W_{si,-1}=1\), and
\(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\),
\[
 W_{si,-1}\prod_{h=0}^{H}\{1+R_{sih}(a)\}
 =1\cdot B_{si}(a)\prod_{h=1}^{H}1
 =B_{si}(a),
\]
where the last product is empty and equals one when \(H=0\).  The prescribed
identity \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) is
\texttt{ass:consistency}.  Centering of \(\eta_{si}\), together with its
independence from \(z_0\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0\mathbb E[\eta_{si}\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s}),
\]
which is \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}.

For boundedness, first suppose \(\kappa=1\) and write
\(y=x_1-1/2\).  Since \(y\in[-1/2,1/2]\),
\[
 -\frac14\le y+y^2\le\frac34,
 \qquad
 \frac{15a_0}{4}\le m_1(x)\le\frac{19a_0}{4}.
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), the two one-sided terms cannot be nonzero
simultaneously, and consequently
\[
 \frac{7a_0}{2}\le m_1(x)\le5a_0.
\]
Every other surface equals \(4a_0\).  Since both noise arrays take values in
\(\{-1,1\}\), these bounds imply
\[
 |Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|
 \le6a_0
 \le\frac{6B}{64}<B.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds.  The response noise is nonzero because,
with \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T})\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(B_{si}(a)\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0.
\]

We now verify \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  If \(0<\lambda<1\), then
\(\kappa=\lambda\).  For \(a,b\ge0\), differentiation of
\(\phi(t)=(1+t)^\lambda-1-t^\lambda\) gives
\(\phi'(t)=\lambda\{(1+t)^{\lambda-1}-t^{\lambda-1}\}\le0\) for
\(t>0\), while \(\phi(0)=0\).  After rescaling, this proves
\((a+b)^\lambda\le a^\lambda+b^\lambda\).  Applying this inequality to
the larger and smaller of \(v_+\) and \(w_+\), and using that the positive-part
map is one-Lipschitz, yields
\[
 |v_+^\lambda-w_+^\lambda|\le |v-w|^\lambda,
 \qquad
 |(-v)_+^\lambda-(-w)_+^\lambda|\le |v-w|^\lambda.
\]
When \(v\) and \(w\) have opposite signs, each of \(|v|\) and \(|w|\)
is at most \(|v-w|\), so the asymmetric cusp has H\"older constant at most
\(3/2\).  As \(|x_1-x'_1|\le\|x-x'\|_2\),
\[
 \|m_1\|_\infty+[m_1]_\lambda
 \le5a_0+\frac32a_0
 =\frac{13}{2}a_0<L.
\]
If \(\lambda\ge1\), the selected surface is quadratic, and its only nonzero
derivatives of positive order are
\[
 \partial_1m_1(x)=a_0\{1+2(x_1-1/2)\},
 \qquad
 \partial_{11}m_1(x)=2a_0.
\]
The first derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\) and is Lipschitz with constant
\(2a_0\); the second derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\); and every derivative
of order greater than two vanishes.  For \(1<\lambda<2\), Lipschitzness and
\(|x_1-x'_1|\le1\) imply the required \((\lambda-1)\)-H\"older bound on the
first derivative.  For \(\lambda>2\), the highest derivative required by the
H\"older norm is constant or zero.  At integer \(\lambda\), the stated
order-reduction convention gives the same bounds.  Thus the standard
isotropic H\"older norm is at most
\[
 \frac{19}{4}a_0+2a_0+2a_0<9a_0<L.
\]
The constant surfaces have norm \(4a_0<L\).  Hence every \(m_s\) belongs to
\(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\).  The first surface is non-affine: it has a
nonzero quadratic term when \(\kappa=1\) and an asymmetric cusp when
\(0<\kappa<1\).

The \(X_{st}\) are independent and uniform on \([0,1]^d\), so their common
density is \(f_X(x)=1\).  Because \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), this is
\texttt{ass:design-density}.  Furthermore,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:interior-path}.  Independence across calendar
windows makes the joint calendar sequence independent, and hence
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\qquad(k\ge1).
\]
This is \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.

Conditional on \((z_0,\mathcal X)\), centering and independence of the noises
give
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
These are exactly the two equalities in
\texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  Conditional on
\((z_0,\mathcal X)\), each unit history is generated by that unit's own
\((\varepsilon_{sti})_{t=1}^{T}\) and \(\eta_{si}\).  Their mutual
independence across \((s,i)\) proves
\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  The construction records each
\(X_{st}\) directly, which is \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.

Finally, define
\[
 \mathcal Z=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}),
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{panel}}
 =\sigma((X_{st},Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i}).
\]
Under the product-law construction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp},
\(\mathcal Z\) is generated by the donor Rademacher array, whereas
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{panel}}\) is generated by the independent design,
training-noise, and event-noise arrays.  Therefore, for every
\(A\in\mathcal Z\) and \(C\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{panel}}\),
\[
 \mathbb P(A\cap C\mid z_0)
 =\mathbb P(A\mid z_0)\mathbb P(C\mid z_0).
\]
This is the full donor-versus-joint-panel factorization required by the
clarified \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}.  All member conditions of
\texttt{def:panel-model-class} have now been verified, and hence
\[
 P_{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}.
\]

It remains to prove the asserted local-modulus order from
\texttt{def:local-modulus}.  For \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), set
\[
 u_\delta=\frac{\delta\Sigma\bar e}{q_0}.
\]
Since \(q_0^2=\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e\),
\[
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2^2
 =\frac{\delta^2}{q_0^2}\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e
 =\delta^2,
 \qquad
 \bar e^{\top}u_\delta=\delta q_0>0.
\]
The radius restriction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} also yields
\[
 \|u_\delta\|_\infty
 \le\delta_0\|\Sigma\bar e/q_0\|_\infty
 \le\frac12.
\]
Because \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), it follows that
\(z_0+u_\delta\in([0,1]^d)^S\).  Thus \(u_\delta\) is feasible in the
supremum defining \(\omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\).

If \(\kappa=1\), the stacked gradient of the weighted surface at \(z_0\) is
\(\pi_1a_0\bar e\), whose covariance-standardized dual norm is
\[
 \|\Sigma^{1/2}(\pi_1a_0\bar e)\|_2
 =\pi_1a_0q_0>0.
\]
Writing \(u_{\delta,s}\) for the cohort-\(s\) block of \(u_\delta\), direct
substitution gives
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0(q_0\delta+q_0^2\delta^2)
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0}{64}\delta+O(\delta^2).
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), positivity of
\(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta\) selects the positive cusp branch, and
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0q_0^\kappa\delta^\kappa
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0^\kappa}{64}\delta^\kappa.
\]
Since \(a_0>0\), \(q_0>0\), and \(\pi_1>0\), these displays give a constant
\(c_{\mathrm{ex}}>0\), depending only on the fixed displayed parameters,
such that
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)
 \ge c_{\mathrm{ex}}\delta^\kappa
 \qquad(0<\delta\le\delta_0).
\]

For the reverse inequality, let \(u\) be any feasible perturbation in
\texttt{def:local-modulus}.  By the upper ellipticity bound,
\[
 \|u\|_2
 =\|\Sigma^{1/2}\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
Put \(v=\bar e^{\top}u\).  Feasibility of \(z_0+u\) gives
\(|v|\le1/2\), and also \(|v|\le\|u\|_2\).  When \(\kappa=1\),
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 =a_0|v+v^2|
 \le\frac32a_0|v|
 \le\frac32a_0C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
When \(0<\kappa<1\), either branch of the asymmetric cusp gives
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 \le a_0|v|^\kappa
 \le a_0C_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\delta^\kappa.
\]
All other cohort surfaces are constant and \(0<\pi_1\le1\).  Taking the
supremum over feasible \(u\), we obtain a finite constant
\(C_{\mathrm{ex}}>0\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)
 \le C_{\mathrm{ex}}\delta^\kappa
 \qquad(0<\delta\le\delta_0).
\]
Combining the last two bounds proves
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^\kappa
 \qquad\text{as }\delta\downarrow0.
\]
The lower bound was derived only for this explicit law; it was not imposed as
a condition on every member of the base H\"older class.

Put \(q=Sd\) and
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad
 D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.
\tag{1}
\]
We first work in the deterministic experiment
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) of
\texttt{def:fixed-design-induced-experiment}.  Fix a parameter point
\(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\).  Conditional on the donor sample, define
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The donor sample is independent of the sigma-field generated by all unit
histories by the definition of the experiment.  Hence conditioning on the
donor-selected indices does not change either mean in (2), and
\(\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}(U_{si}\mid (Z_j)_j)=0\).  The histories are
independent across \((s,i)\), again by the definition of the experiment, so
the variables in (2) are conditionally independent across \((s,i)\).
Bounded support and \(\lVert f_s\rVert_\infty\vee|\mu_s|\le B\) give
\(|U_{si}|\le4B\).  Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\!\left(
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)_j\right)
 \le16B^2A.
\tag{3}
\]

Let \(t_s^0\) be the smallest nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  The
definition of \(t_{s\ell}\), followed twice by the triangle inequality,
gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \lVert X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\rVert_2
 &\le \lVert X_{s,t_s^0}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\rVert_2
       +\lVert\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\rVert_2\\
 &\le \rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\lVert z_s-z_{0s}\rVert_2
       +2\lVert\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\rVert_2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
Because \(0<\lambda\le1\), the map \(x\mapsto x^\lambda\) is
subadditive on \([0,\infty)\).  The Holder restriction in the experiment
therefore implies
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda
 +\lVert z_s-z_{0s}\rVert_2^\lambda
 +\lVert\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\rVert_2^\lambda\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Projection onto the closed cube is nonexpansive because \(z\) belongs to
that cube.  Every balanced fold has \(|I_\ell|\ge N/3\), and the covariance
restriction in the experiment yields
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\lVert\widetilde z_\ell-z\rVert_2^2
 \le \frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le \frac{3SdC_\Sigma}{N}.
\tag{6}
\]
The local parameter restriction also gives
\(\lVert z-z_0\rVert_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).  Expanding
\(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\) into the centered
sum in (3) and the approximation errors in (5), and then applying Jensen's
inequality to (6), gives
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}.
\tag{7}
\]
By \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}, the right-hand side
of (7) is at most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)\).  The first minimax
inequality follows because \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}\) is one admissible
data-measurable estimator.

We next prove the converse.  We shall repeatedly use the following elementary
inequality, which we derive here.  If probability laws \(P_0,P_1\) have
targets separated by \(\Delta>0\) and
\(\lVert P_1-P_0\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1-\eta\), let
\(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\).  The triangle inequality
shows that the squared error under \(P_0\) is at least \(\Delta^2/4\) on
\(A_0^c\), whereas the squared error under \(P_1\) is at least
\(\Delta^2/4\) on \(A_0\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}
 \ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8},
\tag{8}
\]
where the last inequality is the variational definition of total variation.

For the treated-mean channel, fix all response and donor coordinates and,
under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), take the \(E_{si}\)'s independently in
\(\{-b,b\}\), with \(0<b<B\), according to
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(A\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), a sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma>0\)
makes every probability lie in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The two targets are separated
by \(4\gamma\sqrt A\).  The Hellinger affinity of the product laws equals
\[
 \prod_{s=1}^{S}(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge \exp(-C\gamma^2/b^2)>0.
\tag{10}
\]
Indeed, the inequality follows from \(\log(1-x)\ge-Cx\) for
\(0\le x\le1/4\) and
\(\sum_s n_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  For densities \(p,q\),
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to
\(|p-q|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)\) gives
\(\lVert P-Q\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le\{1-(\int\sqrt{pq})^2\}^{1/2}\).  Thus (8)--(10) give risk at least
\(cA\).

For the fixed-design channel, let
\[
 q_s(x)=a_0\min_{1\le t\le T}\lVert x-X_{st}\rVert_2^\lambda,
\]
where \(a_0>0\) is sufficiently small in terms of \(B,L,d\).  Distance to
a set is one-Lipschitz and
\(|u^\lambda-v^\lambda|\le|u-v|^\lambda\) for \(u,v\ge0\), so
\(f_s=q_s/2\) and \(g_s=-q_s/2\) belong to the required Holder ball and
are bounded by \(B\).  They agree at every design site.  Take deterministic
responses equal to zero, identical event laws, and identical donor laws at
center \(z_0\).  The two observed laws are identical, while their targets
differ by
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s q_s(z_{0s})=a_0D_X.
\tag{11}
\]
Equation (8) therefore gives risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

It remains to obtain the donor channel for the prescribed full covariance.
Assume now \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>q^2\).  Choose a signed coordinate
vector \(e\) for which a sufficiently small positive displacement from
\(z_0\) remains in the trimmed cube, and put
\(w=\Sigma^{-1/2}e/\lVert\Sigma^{-1/2}e\rVert_2\).  The construction in
\texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} supplies a standardized
three-point coordinate with mean \(u\), variance one, common support, and
strict fourth-moment slack.  Rotate its first coordinate onto \(w\), leave
the other standardized coordinates as independent Rademacher variables,
and transform by \(\Sigma^{1/2}\).  For \(u=0\) and
\(u=c_*N^{-1/2}\), the donor means are
\[
 z_0,
 \qquad
 z_0+\frac{c_*N^{-1/2}}{\lVert\Sigma^{-1/2}e\rVert_2}e.
\tag{12}
\]
Their covariance is exactly \(\Sigma\), their standardized fourth moments
remain below \(B^4\), and the squared standardized displacement in (12) is
\(c_*^2/N\).  The Hellinger calculation in
\texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} is invariant under the rotation
and invertible linear transformation, so a sufficiently small fixed
\(c_*>0\) makes the product total variation at most \(1-\eta_0\).  Ellipticity
makes the Euclidean displacement in (12) comparable to \(N^{-1/2}\).  A
common affine regression when \(\lambda=1\), or a common one-sided
\(\lambda\)-cusp oriented along \(e\) when \(0<\lambda<1\), can be scaled
into the Holder ball and separates the two values of the regression by
\(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  The response and event laws are otherwise identical.
Equation (8) gives risk at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Taking the maximum of
the three channel bounds and invoking the two-sided characterization in
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} proves
\[
 cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \le \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2.
\tag{13}
\]
The strict interior and moment conditions are used only for this regular
donor-location construction.

We now establish the causal bridge.  Let
\(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{st})_{s,t})\), let \(\mathcal H\) be generated by
all unit training and event histories, and let
\(\mathcal Z=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  The clarified
\texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} states
\(\mathcal Z\) is conditionally independent of
\(\mathcal X\vee\mathcal H\) given \(z_0\).  Thus, for bounded
\(\mathcal Z\)-measurable \(U\) and bounded \(\mathcal H\)-measurable
\(V\), conditional factorization and the tower property give
\[
 \mathbb E(UV\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 =\mathbb E(U\mid z_0)\mathbb E(V\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{14}
\]
Therefore further conditioning on the exact design preserves both the donor
i.i.d. law and its independence from the complete collection of unit
histories.  Together with \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering},
\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}, boundedness, and the donor moment and
ellipticity restrictions, (14) shows that the observed regular conditional
kernel, with its induced mean, regression, and path labels, is a member of
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for \(P\)-almost every realized \(X\).  No
kernel is selected at a null design.  By
\texttt{lem:causal-identification}, its statistical target equals
\(\tau(z_0)\).  Applying (7) to this almost-sure kernel proves the asserted
causal conditional upper bound.

If every cohort design contains \(z_{0s}\), then \(D_X=0\), and the exact-site
conclusion follows directly from
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}.  Finally, suppose
\(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every cohort.  Then
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every foldwise anchor search.  The
selected certificate is no larger than the certificate at that comparison
pair, so
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &C_H\lVert\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\rVert_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le
 C_H\lVert z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\rVert_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
\]
The bandwidth floor implies
\((Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Since \(r=0\),
each fit is a convex combination of the bounded responses; its weights are
nonnegative and sum to one, so clipping is inactive.  Holder continuity
bounds its conditional approximation error by the first two terms on the
left of (15).  Conditional independence across units bounds the variance of
the weighted within-unit contrasts by \(CA\).  Applying (6) with \(z=z_0\),
Jensen's inequality, and (15) therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2
 \mid z_0,(X_{st})]\le CR_D.
\tag{16}
\]
The final comparison \(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\) is the last assertion of
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}.  No reverse comparison
with the Gram certificate has been used.

Write
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad
 D_T=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{2\lambda/d}.
\tag{1}
\]
On the event that the attained anchor at \(z_0\) is coercive, the comparison
argument (15)--(16) in \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} applies; this also
covers the case in which the genuinely attained bandwidth is one.  If the
anchor at \(z_0\) is unavailable, squared error is at most \(16B^2\) because
the estimator and target both lie in \([-2B,2B]\).  The fixed-scale occupancy
part of \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} bounds the probability of
this event by \(CT^{-2}\).  Minkowski's inequality, followed by the two
moment conclusions of that lemma, therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \le C\bigg[&A+
 \left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2\\
 &+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\bigg]
 \le CR_\star.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
Here \(T^{-2}\le CD_T\), because \(0<2\lambda/d\le2\).  The use of the
clarified donor assumption inside the conditional comparison is legitimate
by the factorization (14) proved in \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}.

The apparent smoothing component is redundant.  With
\(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\), direct exponent arithmetic and
the weighted arithmetic--geometric inequality yield
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
 \le2S\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
      +2T^{-2\lambda/d}
 \le C(A+D_T).
\tag{4}
\]

Assume now \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\).  Each lower bound below is
an embedded subexperiment of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  For the
treated-mean channel, use independent uniform exact designs, a common
admissible donor law independent of the entire joint panel, and constant
untreated surfaces.  Translate the two-point outcomes (9) in
\texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} into a fixed positive subinterval of
\((0,B)\).  Set treated potential wealth equal to the observed translated
outcome and untreated event wealth equal to the constant surface.  Taking
\(W_{si,-1}=1\), the horizon-zero return equal to wealth minus one, and all
later returns zero verifies \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  All model assumptions
hold, including donor independence from the full joint panel, and the
two-law inequality (8) in \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} gives risk at
least \(cA\).

The construction in \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} gives two
base-class laws with risk at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  For a fixed auxiliary
error probability in \((0,1/2)\),
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} gives two base-class
laws with a common subprobability measure of positive mass and target
separation \(cD_T^{1/2}\).  Applying the same elementary two-law inequality
gives risk at least \(cD_T\).  The largest of these three bounds, together
with (4), proves
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \asymp A\vee D_T\vee N^{-\lambda}\asymp R_\star.
\tag{5}
\]

On the independent-calendar subclass, the independent part of
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} replaces \(D_T\) in (2) by
\(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For the matching converse, place a cube of radius
\(r_T=cT^{-1/d}\) around \(z_{01}\), and choose two uniformly bounded Holder
regressions which coincide off that cube and differ at its center by
\(c_1r_T^\lambda\).  The density upper bound gives hit probability at most
\(C_Xv_dr_T^d\) for each design point.  Calendar independence and a
sufficiently small fixed \(c\) imply
\[
 \Pr\{X_{1t}\text{ misses the cube for every }t\}
 =(1-p_T)^T\ge c_2>0.
\tag{6}
\]
On this event the two observed response laws coincide, while their targets
differ by \(c_1T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Restricting their common law to this event
and applying (8) from \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} proves the lower
squared-risk term \(cT^{-2\lambda/d}\).

Finally, set \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\).  Formula (2)
then has the unreduced bookkeeping form
\[
 n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}
 \vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
Formula (4) proves that its second term is dominated by the maximum of its
first and third terms, giving the asserted three nonredundant phases and the
stated oracle/generated-proxy boundary.

By \texttt{lem:causal-identification}, the target is the stated observed-law
functional.  Bounded wealth implies \(\tau(z_0)\in[-2B,2B]\).  We first
prove coverage on the regular branch.  Because \(0<\lambda\le1\), one has
\(r=0\).  Conditional on the exact design and donor sample, all selected
local-constant weights are response-independent, nonnegative, and sum to
one.  Hence their bounded-response fits already lie in \([-B,B]\), so the
clipping operation is inactive.  For every \((s,i)\), define
\[
 \xi_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left[
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)
 -\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}\right].
\tag{1}
\]
The clarified \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} makes the donor sample
conditionally independent of the entire joint panel given \(z_0\).
Therefore further conditioning on the donor sample and the exact design
does not change the conditional law of a unit history.  The two equalities
in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} center (1), and
\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes these variables independent
across \((s,i)\).  Their range lengths are at most
\[
 \frac{2B\pi_s}{n_s}\left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right).
\tag{2}
\]
For completeness, if a random variable \(V\) is supported on \([a,b]\),
convexity of the exponential on this interval gives
\(\mathbb E\exp\{u(V-\mathbb EV)\}\le
\exp\{u^2(b-a)^2/8\}\).  Exponential Markov optimization and (2) thus show
that the two-sided unit-history sampling error exceeds
\(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) with conditional probability at most
\[
 2\exp\{-4\log(8/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/4.
\tag{3}
\]
The nonnegative linear bounded-range term in \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) only
enlarges this valid radius.

We next verify the calendar alternative in the definition of the interval.
Each retained score block is excluded from the response observations used by
its cross-fit.  By the total-variation definition of absolute regularity,
replacing one retained block by its product-law copy changes the relevant
joint probability by at most the intervening beta coefficient.  Repeating
this replacement over the two block parities and using the triangle
inequality for total variation changes the joint law by at most
\[
 2SK_T\beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}.
\tag{4}
\]
This is a direct finite telescoping argument, not an asymptotic independence
claim.  Under the resulting product law, the range length of retained block
\(k\) is at most \(L_k\).  Applying the bounded-variable exponential bound
used above separately to the two parities, and then restoring the original
law with (4), gives response-score failure probability at most
\(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2\) by the scalar defining inequality for
\(x_{\mathrm{cal}}\), after adding the deterministic discarded-index bound
\(L_{\mathcal G}\).  A separate use of (2) for the treated replicates gives
\[
 \Pr\{|\text{treated-mean error}|>r_B\mid z_0\}
 \le2\exp\{-4\log(16/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/4.
\tag{5}
\]
Consequently the sampling error exceeds \(r_{\mathrm{cal}}\) with probability
at most \(3\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/4\).  Since
\(r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}\wedge r_{\mathrm{cal}}\), the event
that the error exceeds \(r_{\mathrm{samp}}\) is contained in the union of
the two error events just bounded.  Equations (3)--(5) therefore give total
sampling failure probability at most \(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}\).

For the donor radius, spectral clipping gives
\(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I_{Sd}\).  Projection is nonexpansive,
every fold has \(|I_\ell|\ge N/3\), and donor unbiasedness and ellipticity
imply, without requiring independence between the sample mean and covariance,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[N\left\lVert\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}
 (\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\right\rVert_2^2\mathrel{\Big|}z_0\right]
 \le\frac{6SdC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.
\tag{6}
\]
Markov's inequality and a union bound over at most two folds, with the stated
value of \(q_{\mathrm{don}}\), yield
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\max_\ell
 \left\lVert\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}
 (\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\right\rVert_2
 >q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\mathrel{\Big|}z_0\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{7}
\]
On the complement of (7), the upper spectral clipping bound and projection
onto the cube give
\(\max_\ell\lVert\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\rVert_2\le CN^{-1/2}\).
Holder continuity, the local-constant bias calculation, and the selected
certificate then bound the deterministic approximation error by
\(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\), by the defining choice of the
calibration constant \(C_H\).  Combining the sampling event with (7) and
\(\alpha=\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\) proves coverage on
the regular branch.  On every declared bad branch the interval is
\([-2B,2B]\), which contains the target.  Intersecting a covering interval
with this known target range preserves coverage.  This proves the asserted
uniform conditional coverage, in fact with the stated asymptotic conclusion
following from these finite-sample branchwise bounds.

We next bound expected length.  On the regular branch,
\(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\), and hence
\[
 r_{\mathrm{unit}}\le C(\alpha,B)A^{1/2},
 \qquad r_{\mathrm{samp}}\le r_{\mathrm{unit}}.
\tag{8}
\]
Whenever the anchor comparison at \(z_0\) is available, selected-certificate
optimality and the bandwidth floor give
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}
 \le C\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{(h_s^\star)^\lambda+
 K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \lVert\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\rVert_2^\lambda\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection nonexpansiveness, and Jensen's
inequality imply
\(\mathbb E(\lVert\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\rVert_2^\lambda\mid z_0)
\le CN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Taking expectations in (9) and applying
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\mid z_0)
 \le C\bigg[&\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 +\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\bigg].
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Along the stated growth arrays, every deterministic small-sample bad branch
eventually disappears.  The fixed-scale occupancy argument in the anchor
moment lemma bounds the remaining missing-anchor probability by \(CT^{-2}\).
The interval length is always at most \(4B\), so this event contributes only
\(CT^{-2}\).  Equations (8)--(10), together with smoothing domination (3)--(4)
in \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram}, yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P\{\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid z_0\}
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
Under calendar independence, the independent part of the anchor-moment lemma
replaces the logarithmic term by \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).

For the converse, suppose two laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) possess
a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\).  Uniform
conditional coverage \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under both laws and the union bound
inside \(\nu\) imply
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}
 \ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).
\]
Every interval containing both targets has length at least their separation,
so
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.
\tag{12}
\]
Choose the displacement in the treated two-point family (9) of
\texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} small enough that its common mass exceeds
\(2\alpha\); (12) gives \(cA^{1/2}\).  Under the strict interior and moment
slack, the displacement multiplier in
\texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} can similarly be chosen small
enough that the common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\), while retaining target
separation \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  The construction in
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies common mass
above \(2\alpha\) and separation
\(c\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  Applying (12) to each pair and taking
the largest channel, then using smoothing domination, proves the stated
lower bound \(cR_\star^{1/2}\) for all sufficiently large indices.  The
independent-calendar no-hit construction (6) in
\texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram}, with its cube chosen small enough that
the common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\), gives the asserted
\(T^{-\lambda/d}\) analogue.

Let \(q=Sd\) and \(\Delta_B=B^4-q^2>0\).  Choose \(a_D>1\) such that
\[
 1<a_D^2<1+\Delta_B/2.
\tag{1}
\]
For \(|u|\) in a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of zero, define a
random variable \(V_u\) on \(\{-a_D,0,a_D\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}+\frac{u}{2a_D},
 \qquad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}-\frac{u}{2a_D},
 \qquad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a_D^2}.
\tag{2}
\]
All three probabilities are positive after shrinking the neighborhood.
Direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=u,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(V_u)=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Let the remaining \(q-1\) coordinates be independent Rademacher variables.
At \(u=0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\lVert V_0^{(q)}\rVert_2^4
 =a_D^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2-1+a_D^2<B^4.
\tag{4}
\]
The centered fourth moment is a continuous function of \(u\), so the strict
inequality persists on a smaller fixed neighborhood.

Put \(z^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_q\) and
\(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\delta_Ne_1\), where
\(\delta_N=c_*N^{-1/2}\).  Since \(\delta_0<1/2\), both paths satisfy
\texttt{ass:interior-path} for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Under
alternative \(v\in\{0,1\}\), take i.i.d. donors whose first coordinate is
\(1/2+V_{v\delta_N}\) and whose other coordinates are \(1/2\) plus the
common Rademacher coordinates.  Equations (3)--(4) give
\[
 \mathbb E_vZ_j=z^{(v)},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_v(Z_j)=I_q,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_v\lVert Z_j-z^{(v)}\rVert_2^4\le B^4.
\tag{5}
\]
Because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), (5) verifies the full covariance
ellipticity condition.

The square roots of the three positive probabilities in (2) have bounded
derivatives near zero.  The mean-value theorem therefore gives \(C_0<\infty\)
such that the one-donor squared Hellinger distance between parameters zero
and \(\delta_N\) is at most \(C_0\delta_N^2\).  If
\(\mathcal A(P,Q)=\int\sqrt{dP\,dQ}\) is Hellinger affinity, product
factorization and the Cauchy--Schwarz total-variation bound give
\[
 \lVert P_1^{Z,N}-P_0^{Z,N}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\left\{1-(1-C_0\delta_N^2)^{2N}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Choosing the fixed \(c_*>0\) sufficiently small makes (6) at most
\(1-\eta_0\) for a fixed \(\eta_0>0\).

Use a common i.i.d. uniform exact training design.  If \(0<\kappa<1\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)_+^\kappa;
\]
if \(\kappa=1\), set
\(m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)\).  Set all other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).
Positive constants \(b_0,b_1\), chosen sufficiently small in terms of
\(B,L\), put these surfaces in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), keep them
strictly inside \([-B,B]\), and imply
\[
 |m_1(z^{(1)}_1)-m_1(z^{(0)}_1)|=b_1\delta_N^\kappa.
\tag{7}
\]
Use the same bounded centered response noise, the same training design, and
the same positive constant treated observations under both alternatives.
Thus the complete observed joint panel law is identical under the two laws.
Set \(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and set the unobserved untreated
event wealth to the constant \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\).  All amplitudes can be
chosen in \((0,B)\).  With \(W_{si,-1}=1\),
\(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\),
\texttt{def:buyhold-level} reproduces these wealth levels.

The construction verifies consistency, event-date transport, boundedness,
Holder smoothness, conditional centering, cross-unit independence, and
geometric mixing.  It also makes the donor sample conditionally independent
of the entire joint panel
\(((X_{st},Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i})\), exactly as
required by the clarified \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}.  Donor
i.i.d. sampling, unbiasedness, ellipticity, and the fourth-moment restriction
follow from (5).  Thus both laws belong to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  Finally,
\texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (7) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z^{(1)})-\tau_0(z^{(0)})|
 =\pi_1b_1c_*^\kappa N^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{8}
\]
The panel factors are identical and (6) controls the only differing observed
factor, proving the asserted two-law certificate without a class-wide lower
local-modulus condition.

Put \(q=Sd\).  The condition \(B^4\ge q^2\) permits the common donor law
\(Z_j=z_0+U_j\), where the coordinates of \(U_j\) are independent
Rademacher variables.  It has mean \(z_0\), covariance \(I_q\), and
standardized fourth moment
\(\mathbb E\lVert U_j\rVert_2^4=q^2\).  We take it independent of the
entire joint panel, so all clarified donor-separation requirements hold.

Choose \(\gamma>0\) so small that \(e^{-\gamma}>2\alpha\), and put
\[
 L_T=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\log T-2\log\log(T\vee3)}{|\log\rho_0|}
 \right\rfloor\vee1,
 \qquad
 p_T=\frac{\gamma L_T}{T}.
\tag{1}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), elementary exponentiation of the
definition of \(L_T\) gives
\[
 2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
Partition the first cohort's calendar into consecutive complete blocks of
length \(L_T\), and independently label each complete block by
\(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Let \(A_T\) be a cube centered
at \(z_{01}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_d\) with volume \(p_T\).  Conditional on
\(C_b=1\), draw every design point in block \(b\) independently uniformly
on \(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently uniformly on
its complement.  At each complete-block time the marginal density is
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Draw the incomplete block and every other cohort independently and uniformly.
Thus the design-density bounds hold.

If \(k<L_T\), past and future sigma-fields separated by \(k\) indices can
share at most one block label.  In the total-variation definition of
absolute regularity, replacing this Bernoulli label by an independent copy
changes their joint law by at most \(2p_T\).  If \(k\ge L_T\), the sigma-fields
involve disjoint labels and are independent.  Because \(k\le L_T-1\) in the
first case, (2) gives
\[
 \beta(k)\le2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
 \le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k<L_T,
\tag{4}
\]
and the same bound is trivial for \(k\ge L_T\).

Let \(E_T\) be the event that every complete-block label vanishes and that no
point in the incomplete block falls in a fixed smaller concentric cube.  The
incomplete-block failure probability is at most \(L_Tp_T=o(1)\), while
\[
 \Pr(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}-o(1)
 \longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}>
 \eta_\alpha:=\frac{e^{-\gamma}+2\alpha}{2}>2\alpha.
\tag{5}
\]
Let \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\) be the side scale of the smaller cube.  Choose a
fixed smooth bump \(\phi\), supported inside that cube after rescaling, with
\(\phi(0)=1\).  For sufficiently small fixed \(a,b_0>0\), define
\[
 m_{10}(x)=b_0,
 \qquad
 m_{11}(x)=b_0+ah_T^\lambda
 \phi((x-z_{01})/h_T),
\tag{6}
\]
and keep every other surface equal to \(b_0\).  Derivatives of order \(j\)
scale as \(h_T^{\lambda-j}\), while the highest-order Holder seminorm is
scale invariant.  Hence the two functions lie uniformly in
\(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\); small \(a,b_0\) also enforce bounded wealth.

Under alternative \(v\), set \(Q_{1ti}=m_{1v}(X_{1t})\), use the common
constant surfaces elsewhere, keep positive treated observations identical,
impose consistency, and set unobserved untreated event wealth equal to
\(m_{sv}(z_{0s})\).  Taking baseline wealth one, the horizon-zero return
equal to wealth minus one, and every later return zero realizes these
positive wealth levels under \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  Design-conditional
centering and transport hold by construction; conditional on the design the
unit histories are degenerate and hence mutually independent.  The joint
design--response sequence inherits (4), and the donor sample is independent
of the entire joint panel.  Thus both laws belong to the frozen model class.

On \(E_T\), no response is evaluated in the bump support.  The restrictions
of the two observed laws to \(E_T\) therefore coincide, giving a common
subprobability measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\) for all sufficiently
large \(T\).  Finally, \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (6) imply
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|
 =\pi_1ah_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d},
\tag{7}
\]
which proves the claimed common-submeasure certificate.

Because \(0<\lambda\le1\), the order convention gives \(r=0\), so the
local-polynomial Gram matrix is scalar.  Continuity of \(K\) and its strict
positivity on a smaller ball provide constants \(k_0>0\) and
\(\eta\in(0,1)\) such that \(K(v)\ge k_0\) whenever
\(\lVert v\rVert_2\le\eta\).  Interiority and the density lower bound, in
the conditional law at the fixed \(z_0\), give for
\(b\le\delta_0/\eta\)
\[
 p_b:=\Pr\{\lVert X_{st}-z_{0s}\rVert_2\le\eta b\mid z_0\}
 \ge c_Xv_d\eta^db^d=:c_pb^d.
\tag{1}
\]
If \(M_b\) counts these visits, then the definition of \(G_{sT}\) gives
\[
 G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\ge\frac{k_0M_b}{Tb^d}.
\tag{2}
\]

Divide the calendar into consecutive blocks of length \(a_T\), and split
the complete blocks by parity.  Blocks in either parity are separated by at
least \(a_T\) observations.  By the total-variation definition of absolute
regularity, replacing one retained block by its product-law copy changes the
expectation of every function bounded by one by at most the intervening beta
coefficient.  Iteration and the triangle inequality over both parities give
the finite bound
\[
 2\left\lceil\frac{T}{a_T}\right\rceil
 \beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}\le CT^{-2},
\tag{3}
\]
because \(\rho_0^{a_T}\le(T\vee2)^{-3}\).

For an independent comparison-block count \(Y_j\in[0,a_T]\), convexity of
\(y\mapsto e^{-y/a_T}\) on this interval implies
\[
 \mathbb E(e^{-Y_j/a_T})
 \le1-\frac{1-e^{-1}}{a_T}\mathbb E(Y_j)
 \le\exp\left\{-\frac{1-e^{-1}}{a_T}\mathbb E(Y_j)\right\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Exponential Markov applied to the product comparison law separately for the
two parities, followed by (1), (3), and (4), gives constants
\(c_1,C_1>0\) such that whenever \(Tb^d\ge C_1a_T\),
\[
 \Pr\{M_b\le c_1Tb^d\mid z_0\}
 \le C_1\exp\{-c_1Tb^d/a_T\}+C_1T^{-2}.
\tag{5}
\]
Increasing \(C_1\) makes (5) trivial for smaller \(Tb^d/a_T\).  The stated
compatibility of \(c_G\) with the population local-constant Gram lower bound
makes the right-hand side of (2) at least \(c_G\) on the complement of the
event in (5).

Set
\[
 b_\circ=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}
 \vee N^{-1/2}\vee(a_T/T)^{1/d}.
\tag{6}
\]
Choose at each stage the smallest dyadic candidate not below the indicated
scale; it is within a factor two of that scale.  Applying (5) to candidates
not below a constant multiple of \(2^jb_\circ\), and taking a union bound
over the remaining dyadic candidates, yields
\[
 \Pr\{h_s^\star>C2^jb_\circ\mid z_0\}
 \le C\exp(-c2^{jd})+CT^{-2},
 \qquad j\ge0.
\tag{7}
\]
For scales above a fixed interior radius, the same conclusion follows by
comparison with that fixed radius; if a scale exceeds one it is immediate
from \(h_s^\star\le1\).  Thus no boundary extrapolation is hidden in (7).
Integrating its dyadic tail gives
\[
 \mathbb E[(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}\mid z_0]
 \le Cb_\circ^{2\lambda}+CT^{-2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Since \(a_T\asymp\log(T\vee2)\) and \(2\lambda/d\le2\), equations (6)--(8)
imply
\[
 \mathbb E[(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}\mid z_0]
 \le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}+N^{-\lambda}
 +\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right)^{2\lambda/d}\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \((h_s^\star)^\lambda\) gives the corresponding
first-moment assertion.

At \(b=1\), the intersection of the fixed positivity ball of \(K\) with
the cube has volume bounded below uniformly in the center.  Repeating
(1)--(5) at this fixed scale shows that the event that no coercive candidate
exists at the reference point has probability at most \(CT^{-2}\).  On its
complement, every fold--cohort anchor set contains this same response-free
comparison pair.  A union bound over the fixed number \(SK_N\) therefore
gives
\[
 \sup_P\Pr_P(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0)\le CT^{-2}.
\tag{10}
\]
If the calendar observations are independent, the product comparison above
is exact and one may take \(a_T=1\).  Repeating (6)--(9) then replaces the
last term by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\), as claimed.

Let
\[
 \mathcal X=\sigma\!\left((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T}\right),
 \qquad
 p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0),
 \qquad
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
Because \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth}, and \texttt{ass:consistency} imply \(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) almost surely, so all conditional expectations below exist.  Since \(E\in\mathcal X\), the random variable \(b\mathbf 1_E\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The assumed equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\mathbf 1_E\), valid almost surely under the conditional law given \(z_0\), therefore implies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =b\mathbf 1_E
 \quad\text{almost surely under that conditional law}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
On the other hand, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]
 =\mu_{si}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.                                                                  \tag{2}
\]
Taking conditional expectation given \(z_0\) in the shock representation yields
\[
 \mu_{si}=b\,\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=bp_E.                                           \tag{3}
\]
Combining (1)--(3), squaring, and taking conditional expectation given \(z_0\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
  0
  &=\mathbb E_P[(b\mathbf 1_E-bp_E)^2\mid z_0]\\
  &=b^2\mathbb E_P[(\mathbf 1_E-p_E)^2\mid z_0]\\
  &=b^2p_E(1-p_E).
 \end{aligned}                                                                                  \tag{4}
\]
The last equality uses \(\mathbf 1_E^2=\mathbf 1_E\) and \(\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=p_E\).  Because \(b\ne0\), division by \(b^2\) in (4) gives \(p_E(1-p_E)=0\).  Since a conditional probability belongs to \([0,1]\),
\[
 \Pr_P(E\mid z_0)=p_E\in\{0,1\}.
\]

For the former scalar construction in the statement, \(z_0\) is fixed, \(X_{11}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), \(E=\{X_{11}\le q\}\), and \(q\in(0,1)\).  Therefore
\[
 \Pr_P(E\mid z_0)=\Pr_P(X_{11}\le q\mid z_0)=q\in(0,1).
\]
Taking \(b=b_*>0\) contradicts (4).  Thus the shocked law violates \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}; by the member-property construction in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, it is not an element of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  The former obstruction required the shocked law to belong to that class, so that obstruction is excluded.  Notice that the argument uses the observed-law centering restriction and does not invoke causal event-date transport.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), a cohort \(s\), and a unit \(i\), and put
\[
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
By membership, \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth}, and \texttt{ass:consistency}, \(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) almost surely, so \(\mu_{si}\) is finite.  By \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering},
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=0.                            \tag{5}
\]
Let \(W\) be bounded and \(\mathcal X\)-measurable.  Then \((B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W\) is integrable, and \(W\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The pull-out and tower properties of conditional expectation applied to (5) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W\mid z_0]
 &=\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 W\,\mathbb E_P(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 \mathrel{\Big|}z_0\right]\\
 &=0.
 \end{aligned}                                                                                 \tag{6}
\]
This is the asserted conditional orthogonality.

Now take \(E\in\mathcal X\) and write \(p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0)\).  Substituting \(W=\mathbf 1_E\) into (6) yields
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=\mu_{si}p_E.                          \tag{7}
\]
If \(p_E>0\), division of (7) by \(p_E\), using the definition of conditional expectation on an event, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E]=\mu_{si}.                                     \tag{8}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(E^c\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E^c]=\mu_{si}                                    \tag{9}
\]
whenever \(p_E<1\).  Thus (8)--(9) hold simultaneously when \(0<p_E<1\).  The exclusion of the former common-design-shock experiment is precisely \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction}.

It remains to prove the asserted two-law certificate showing that this centering repair does not itself select the centered event-noise constant.  For arbitrary positive integers \(N,T,n_1\), choose the admissible scalar fixed parameters
\[
 S=1,
 \quad \pi_1=1,
 \quad H=0,
 \quad p=d=1,
 \quad z_0=\frac12,
 \quad \lambda=\kappa=1,
 \quad B=L=1,
 \quad \delta_0=\frac14,
\]
and set \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), with arbitrary fixed \(\beta_0>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  The identity \(d=p(H+1)=1\) and all declared parameter ranges are satisfied.

On a product probability space let \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T}\), \((\xi_j)_{j=1}^{N}\), and \((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1}\) be mutually independent, with
\[
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad
 \Pr(\xi_j=1)=\Pr(\xi_j=-1)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \Pr(\varepsilon_i=1)=\Pr(\varepsilon_i=-1)=\frac12.
\]
Define the untreated regression, training responses, and donor scores by
\[
 m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m_1(X_{1t})=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Z_j=\frac12+\xi_j.                                                                          \tag{10}
\]
For every event unit put \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\) and \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\).  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level},
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.                                                                           \tag{11}
\]
Under \(P^{(0)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\).  Under \(P^{(1)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  Under both laws impose \texttt{ass:consistency} by defining \(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  The buy-and-hold formula then gives
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12
 \quad\text{under }P^{(0)},
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad\text{under }P^{(1)}.                                                                  \tag{12}
\]
All constructed returns belong to \((-1,\infty)\), because their smallest possible value is \(-1/2\).

We verify each member property of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\).  Equations (10)--(12) imply
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(0)|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,
\]
so \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds with \(B=1\).  The constant function \(m_1\) has supremum norm \(1/2\), every positive-order derivative equal to zero, and Holder seminorm zero.  Hence \(m_1\in\mathcal H_1(1,1)\), as required by \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac12,\partial[0,1]\right)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 f_X(x)=1\quad(0\le x\le1),                                                                  \tag{13}
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:interior-path} and \texttt{ass:design-density}.

Conditional on the complete design array, every training outcome in (10) is deterministic.  Under \(P^{(0)}\), the event outcomes are deterministic; under \(P^{(1)}\), unit \(i\)'s event history depends only on \(\varepsilon_i\).  Independence of the \(\varepsilon_i\)'s therefore proves \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  The calendar blocks in (10) are independent over \(t\), so their beta-mixing coefficients satisfy
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1,                                                                               \tag{14}
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  Declaring each \(X_{1t}\) in (10) directly observed verifies \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T})\).  Equation (10) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Q_{1ti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =m_1(X_{1t}).                                                                                \tag{15}
\]
Under either law, (12), independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\), and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].                                               \tag{16}
\]
Thus both clauses of \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} hold.

For the clarified donor-versus-joint-panel factorization, define
\[
 \mathcal D=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}),
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{pan}}
 =\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T},(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i=1}^{n_1}).
\]
By (10), every \(Q_{1ti}\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal X\), while by (12) every event outcome is either constant or measurable with respect to \(\sigma((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1})\).  Consequently,
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{pan}}
 \subseteq\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T},(\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1}),
 \qquad
 \mathcal D\subseteq\sigma((\xi_j)_{j=1}^{N}).
\]
Mutual independence of the three primitive arrays therefore yields
\[
 \mathcal D\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pan}}\mid z_0,                  \tag{17}
\]
where conditioning on \(z_0=1/2\) is conditioning on a constant.  Equation (17) is exactly \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}: it factors the donors from the entire joint panel and imposes no additional restriction on dependence within a unit history.

By (10), conditional on the fixed \(z_0=1/2\), the donor scores are independent and identically distributed and satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid z_0)=1.                                                 \tag{18}
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness} hold.  Since \(c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), (18) proves \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Finally,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 |\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid z_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E[|\xi_j|^4]
 =1
 =B^4,                                                                                        \tag{19}
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} while retaining the full scalar covariance.

Equation (11) and the definition of \(m_1\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]
 =\frac12
 =m_1(z_0),                                                                                  \tag{20}
\]
so \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} holds.  Consistency was imposed before (12).  We have therefore verified every member property listed in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, and hence
\[
 P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}.
\]

The joint law of \(((X_{1t})_t,(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(Z_j)_j)\) is the same under \(P^{(0)}\) and \(P^{(1)}\) by (10) and the common product construction.  By \texttt{def:target}, (11)--(12), and the zero mean of a Rademacher variable,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau_{P^{(0)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{(0)}}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]=0,\\
 \tau_{P^{(1)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{(1)}}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]
 =\frac14\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0.
 \end{aligned}                                                                                \tag{21}
\]
Nevertheless, (12) and independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\) yield
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 =\frac1{16}\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)
 =\frac1{16}.                                                                                \tag{22}
\]
Thus the centered class permits both event-noise constants while holding the training experiment, donor experiment, and causal target fixed.  Equations (5)--(9) prove the asserted orthogonality and eventwise mean invariance, while (10)--(22) provide the explicit two-law certificate under the clarified donor-versus-joint-panel factorization.  Therefore exclusion of the invalid common-design-shock witness is logically distinct from calculation of a sharp minimax constant for the remaining centered product experiment.
